sections.title: Advanced Concept: Digital Sum (Digit Root)
sections.content: Digital sum is the sum of the digits of a number until it becomes a single digit. It is a powerful tool to verify answers in exact simplification. The digital sum of the question equation will ALWAYS equal the digital sum of the correct option. (Note: Cast out 9s to speed this up, as 9 acts like 0 in digital sum).

sections.title: Rules of Surds and Indices
sections.content: Master the laws of exponents. x^a * x^b = x^(a+b); x^a / x^b = x^(a-b); (x^a)^b = x^(ab); x^(a/b) = b-th root of x^a. Questions often equate a massive equation to x^? — here, you must convert all bases to the same prime number.

sections.title: Infinite Nested Roots (Addition/Subtraction)
sections.content: For equations like √(a + √(a + √(a...))), factorize 'a' into two consecutive integers (n * (n+1)). If the sign is '+', the larger integer is the answer. If the sign is '-', the smaller integer is the answer.

sections.title: Infinite Nested Roots (Multiplication)
sections.content: For infinite multiplication series like √(a√(a√(a...))), the answer is simply 'a'. For finite series of 'n' roots like √(a√(a√a)), the formula is a^((2^n - 1) / 2^n).

sections.title: Base Equalization in Decimal Indices
sections.content: When dealing with decimals in powers, convert bases like 0.2, 0.04, 0.008 strictly to 0.2^1, 0.2^2, 0.2^3 to easily equate the powers on the Left Hand Side (LHS) and Right Hand Side (RHS).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Using Digital Sum in 'Approximation' questions (It ONLY works for exact Simplification). 2. Adding powers when bases are different. 3. Dividing the digital sum (Digital sum rules for division require specific fractional conversions).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 bypasses heavy calculation. Use Digital Sum to eliminate options in exact calculations. Convert complex exponents to identical bases, and use standard formulas to instantly collapse infinite surd chains.

tricks.title: Casting Out 9s (Digital Sum)
tricks.explanation: Add digits to a single number. Ignore 9s or combinations that sum to 9. Check if the question's digital sum matches the option's digital sum.
tricks.example: 345 + 124 = ? Digital Sum: (3+4+5=12->3) + (1+2+4=7) = 10->1. The correct option 469 has Digital Sum (4+6+9 -> ignore 9 -> 4+6=10->1). Matches perfectly.

tricks.title: Nested Root Trick (+/-)
tricks.explanation: For √(x + √(x + √(x...∞))), find factors of x with a difference of 1. If +, pick the bigger factor. If -, pick the smaller factor.
tricks.example: √(42 + √(42 + √(42...))). Factors of 42 are 6 x 7. The sign is +, so the answer is 7.

tricks.title: Finite Root Multiplication Trick
tricks.explanation: For a number 'x' under 'n' square roots, the answer is x^( (2^n - 1) / 2^n ).
